question: Obtain the Cartesian equation of the line passing through $A(1,-2,3)$ and $B(4,2,-3)$. Hence, verify whether the point $C(7,6,-9)$ lies on this line.
explanation:
Step 1: Direction components of the line
The direction components obtained from $A(1,-2,3)$ and $B(4,2,-3)$ are
$$4-1=3,\quad 2-(-2)=4,\quad -3-3=-6.$$
Step 2: Cartesian form of the line
A line passing through $(x_1,y_1,z_1)$ with direction ratios $a,b,c$ has Cartesian equation
$$\frac{x-x_1}{a}=\frac{y-y_1}{b}=\frac{z-z_1}{c}.$$
Therefore, the required equation is
$$\frac{x-1}{3}=\frac{y+2}{4}=\frac{z-3}{-6}.$$
Step 3: Substitution of point $C$
For $C(7,6,-9)$,
$$\frac{7-1}{3}=2,\quad \frac{6+2}{4}=2,\quad \frac{-9-3}{-6}=2.$$
Step 4: Verification
All three ratios have the same value. Hence $C$ satisfies the Cartesian equation.
Step 5: Final conclusion
The line is $\frac{x-1}{3}=\frac{y+2}{4}=\frac{z-3}{-6}$, and $C(7,6,-9)$ lies on it.

options.A: $\frac{x-1}{3}=\frac{y+2}{4}=\frac{z-3}{6}$; $C$ does not lie on the line
options.D: $\frac{x-1}{4}=\frac{y+2}{3}=\frac{z-3}{-6}$; $C$ does not lie on the line
